answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens to enter verification clusters. A game-theoretic multi-agent auditing protocol assigns bonded verifiers across an expander graph, where a fraudulent cluster incurs stake slashing. Identifying Sybils relies on topological cut verifications: when fake identities form an insular cluster like a spiral vortex or branching cedar lattice, the graph conductance drops. Detecting this cut forces superlinear attacker cost scaling with network size, making mass spoofing as fragile as shattered marble.
